sources.quote: Rastorfer offers a lengthy biography of Ammann (1879-1965).

label: Arrived in America
description: Ammann traveled to New York to gain practical experience.

sources.quote: He begins his account with the young Swiss engineer's arrival in America in 1904.

label: Graduated from ETH Zurich
description: Graduated from the federal technical university in Zurich before arriving in America.

sources.quote: Having just graduated from the federal technical university (ETH) in Zurich, Ammann traveled to New York in hopes of gaining some practical experience in designing steel bridges.

One learns almost nothing about his character and little about his personal life, only that he wed his childhood sweetheart in 1905, raised three children, and remarried, a year after his wife's death, the widow of a former colleague.

label: Began working for Gustav Lindenthal
description: Started working for the bridge builder Gustav Lindenthal.

sources.quote: In 1911, Ammann began working for Gustav Lindenthal, then considered the "master of long span design" (7);

label: Made chief engineer on Hell Gate project
description: Lindenthal made him chief engineer on the Hell Gate railroad crossing project.

sources.quote: a year later this rather irascible Austrian American bridge builder made him chief engineer on the project to construct a large railroad crossing, the Hell Gate.

label: Lindenthal proposed Hudson river bridge
description: Lindenthal proposed plans for an enormous two-storey span crossing the Hudson river.

sources.quote: In 1920, he proposed plans for an enormous two-storey span that could accommodate railroad, automotive, and pedestrian traffic, estimating its cost at some $100 million.

label: Unveiled proposals for Hudson river bridge
description: Ammann unveiled his proposals for a smaller, cheaper suspension bridge for the Hudson river.

sources.quote: In 1924, Ammann unveiled his proposals for the bridge, a smaller, simpler and, at $40 million, decidedly less costly version of Lindenthal's crossing.

label: Joined Port Authority staff
description: Joined the staff at the Port Authority as bridge engineer.

sources.quote: Ammann thus joined, in 1925, the staff at the Port Authority as bridge engineer.

label: Became United States citizen
description: Became a United States citizen in the same year he joined the Port Authority.

sources.quote: He became a United States citizen later that year.

label: Resigned from Port Authority
description: Turned down a promotion and resigned along with several colleagues.

sources.quote: In 1939, the Port Authority offered (apparently in an attempt to downsize) to "promote" the now sixty year-old Ammann to a more executive position. He turned down the job, resigned along with several colleagues, and established his own firm.

label: Established own firm
description: Established his own engineering firm after resigning from the Port Authority.

sources.quote: He turned down the job, resigned along with several colleagues, and established his own firm.

label: Throgs Neck and Verrazano bridges opened
description: Throgs Neck, Verrazano, and lower deck of George Washington Bridge opened.

sources.quote: Most notably, he designed and oversaw the construction of the Throgs Neck and Verrazano bridges, as well as the lower deck for the then twenty year-old George Washington (all opened in the early 1960s).
He died in 1965, at age eighty-six.

label: Six Bridges published
description: Darl Rastorfer's book on Ammann was published.

sources.quote: Darl Rastorfer, Six Bridges: The Legacy of Othmar Ammann. New Haven and London: Yale University Press, 2000.

label: Review published
description: Nicole Butz's review was published in Swiss American Historical Society Review.

sources.quote: Swiss American Historical Society Review Volume 37 Number 1 Article 5 2-2001
